title: FloorPlanner design document (v5)
description: A floor/site design. The durable unit is the ROOM: it owns an ordered outline of vertices, its furnishings, and its schedule properties. Walls are OPTIONAL bindings onto outline edges — a wall can be deleted, and the room keeps its shape, name, area and contents; the edge simply becomes open. A room whose walls are bound only to itself is `floating` (a concept room, or one extracted from the plan) and can be moved, rotated and duplicated as a unit without touching the rest of the design. All coordinates are plan inches, x right, y down (Qt scene convention); there is no nested coordinate system anywhere in this document. Vertices are the only place coordinates live, so two walls meeting at a corner reference ONE vertex and cannot drift apart.

levels.description: Ordered storeys / site layers, lowest first. Replaces v4 `floors` — renamed so it never reads as floor *finish*.

vertices.description: THE ONLY COORDINATES IN THE DOCUMENT. Every wall end and every room corner is one of these. Sharing a vertex is what makes a corner a corner; nothing else needs a weld tolerance at rest.

walls.description: Built fabric. A wall spans exactly one room-outline edge on each side it serves (walls are split at every vertex any outline uses), so `left`/`right` are single-valued. Identified by its (level, v1, v2) pair — duplicates are invalid, which makes coincident-copy explosions unrepresentable.

rooms.description: The durable unit. Survives the deletion of every wall around it.

provenance.description: How this document came to be, written ONCE at import and never mutated afterwards. Present only on documents converted from a legacy v1-v4 file, where the load-time weld changed real coordinates: it is the audit trail answering 'why is this room a different size than it was in v4?'. Stable, so it is safe to include in the dict equality used for the dirty flag.

endpoints_welded.description: Wall ends moved onto a neighbour by the load-time weld. Non-zero means geometry changed and the document opened dirty.

size_code.description: WWHH / WWWHH / WWWHHH inch size code — "3680" = 36" x 80".

vertex_weld_in.description: MODELLING PRECISION. Two coordinates this close ARE one vertex; a document in which they are not is malformed (invariant I14). Replaces the 0.6/0.75/1.0/1.5/0.02 tolerances scattered through walls.py and rooms.py. Deliberately tiny -- it is a statement about representation, not about the user's aim.

join_tol_in.description: GESTURE TOLERANCE. How close the user must get before the editor OFFERS to weld a dragged end onto a neighbour, and the radius used by the one-time weld when importing a legacy v1-v4 file (config.JOIN_TOL). Never an invariant: a wall deliberately stopping 6" short of another is a legitimate design (a reveal, a pilaster gap), and nothing may silently close it.

area_basis.description: `centerline` reproduces v4. `inside_face` offsets each bound outline edge inward by half its wall's thickness — the number that belongs in a room schedule.

editing_modes.description: Persisted editing behaviour. SHUFFLE MODE is `shuffle: true`, which implies auto_coalesce/auto_weld/auto_bind all off: floating rooms can be dragged past and through each other without their walls merging into the plan or welding to neighbours. Turning shuffle off re-enables the joining passes, and rooms are joined explicitly, not silently.

auto_coalesce.description: Merge collinear same-type walls that meet at a degree-2 vertex.

auto_weld.description: Snap a drawn endpoint onto a nearby existing vertex.

auto_bind.description: Bind a room outline edge to a coincident wall automatically.

kind.description: `site` levels hold landscape work — beds, patios, fences, hedges — and are excluded from conditioned-area totals.

locked.description: Pinned by the user; snapping, welding and cleanup must not move it.

type.description: There is deliberately no `open` type: an outline edge with no wall IS the open edge. Landscape types carry no openings and no finishes.

left.description: Room on the LEFT of the v1->v2 direction — with x right and y down, the (dy, -dx) side, i.e. the side on your left walking v1 to v2 on screen. null = no room that side (outdoors, or a free-standing wall). MAINTAINED INDEX: must agree exactly with which rooms name this wall in their outline (invariant I6).

finish_left.description: Per-side finish. A shared wall can be tile on the bath side and paint on the bedroom side — v4 could not express this because wall_finish lived on the room.

kind.description: `gate` is the landscape counterpart of a door: it is the ONLY opening kind permitted in a fence, hedge, railing or retaining wall (enforced on the wall, below).

anchor.description: Dimensioned the way a drawing dimensions it: an offset from a NAMED END, not an absolute distance from p1. Survives the wall being stretched, split at a new vertex, or reversed — absolute `s` survives none of those.

from.description: `v1`/`v2`: offset from that vertex to the opening's near edge. `center`: offset of the opening centre from the wall midpoint.

sill_in.description: Sill height above the level. Windows only.

door_type.description: Catalog leaf type; meaningful only when kind == "door".

hinge.description: Hinged end, named by vertex so handedness is unambiguous under wall reversal (v4's LH/RH was not).

swings_toward.description: Side the leaf opens into, relative to v1->v2. Replaces the bare swing: -1|1.

outline_edge.description: One step around a room's outline: the corner vertex, plus the wall (if any) running from this vertex to the NEXT vertex in the loop. `wall: null` is an OPEN edge — the room's shape is unchanged, there is simply no built fabric there. Deleting a wall nulls this field; it never deletes the room.

v.description: Corner vertex, in this room's level.

wall.description: Wall spanning v -> next.v. Its endpoints must be exactly {v, next.v}; traversal direction is derived, never stored.

category.description: `site` rooms ARE rooms: a planting bed, lawn zone, patio or gravel court gets an area, a schedule (surface / plant_palette / irrigation / edging), and the same movable-unit behaviour as any interior room. `exterior` covers roofed-but-unconditioned space -- porches, decks, carports. `concept` rooms are sketch units never intended to join the plan and are always `floating`. Overlap (invariant I11) is checked WITHIN a class only: interior+exterior form one class (a porch may not overlap a bedroom), `site` is its own (a lawn zone may pass under a deck), `concept` is exempt.

outline.description: The room's shape: a closed, ordered loop of corner vertices, each optionally carrying the wall on the edge that leaves it. THIS IS THE ROOM'S GEOMETRY AND IT IS INDEPENDENT OF THE WALLS. Area = shoelace of the corners, perimeter = sum of edge lengths, corners = the vertices. Nothing is flood-filled and nothing is cached in `properties`.

holes.description: Inner loops (a courtyard, a chase, a planting bed inside a patio), wound opposite to the outline.

placement.description: Whether this room participates in the shared wall network. DECLARED INTENT, and checked: a `floating` room must be genuinely independent — no wall on its outline may serve a second room, and no vertex it uses may be touched by a wall outside its outline (invariant I12). That is what makes it safe to drag, rotate and duplicate as a unit.

rotation.description: Cumulative rotation applied to this room since it was created, for display and for un-rotating a template. Purely informational: the outline vertices already carry the rotated coordinates.

extracted_from.description: If this room was EXTRACTED from the plan, the level it came from. Lets `rejoin` offer the original context.

area_accounting.description: Which total this room rolls up into. Omitted = derived from `category`: interior -> conditioned, exterior -> unconditioned, site -> site, concept -> excluded. Set explicitly for the exceptions (an unheated sunroom, a garage counted separately).

nominal_size.description: Optional design intent for a room typed in by dimension ("12 x 14 bedroom") rather than drawn. Never authoritative — the outline is. Useful for room templates and for reporting drawn-vs-intended.

offset.description: Relative to the outline centroid, so the label follows the room automatically — v4 stored an absolute anchor that had to be translated by hand at every move site.

room_properties.description: Schedule data only. NO geometry: v4 shadowed the corner list in here as `perimeter_corners`; corners now come from `outline` and storing them here is a schema error.

wall_finish.description: Default for bound walls; a wall's own finish_left/finish_right wins.

surface.description: Site rooms: lawn, mulch, gravel, pavers, decomposed granite, water, planting soil.

plant_palette.description: Site rooms: species / cultivar list for a bed.

irrigation.description: Site rooms: none, drip, spray, rotor, hand.

edging.description: Site rooms: the landscape analogue of baseboard -- steel, stone, bender board, none.

room.description: Owning room, or null for site items (a car, a mower, a tree outside any zone). ASSIGNED when placed, never re-derived — v4 answered this by point-in-polygon in two different places that disagreed (RoomItem used pos(), the inventory dialog used scenePos()). Ownership is what makes a room a movable unit: moving or extracting a room carries exactly the furnishings that name it, including any that a wall deletion would otherwise have stranded.

pos.description: Plan coordinates of the symbol centre.

state.description: Per-kind extra state (stair flight/turn/direction, plant species, …). v4 spread these across the object; nesting keeps the base shape closed.

group.description: A transient named selection set of rooms / walls / furnishings. A group NEVER copies anything: moving it translates the vertices its members reference plus its member furnishings. Rooms are the durable unit; groups are for ad-hoc multi-room moves.
